applies_why: The judge text resolves a Matthew 1:16 link by treating the isolated verse's ambiguity as underdetermined, which is the verse-by-verse adjudication the rule governs.
quote: D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse" — read as allowing an isolated verse's ambiguity to decide the link, versus requiring the pressed chains to be weighed by footing.
why: The judge makes Matthew 1:16's own ambiguity deciding, rather than weighing the defender's and challenger's chains by footing, so it uses the verse-by-verse approach K-C forbids.
